title: Principles of Macroeconomics
description: Sixty original constructed questions for a standalone introductory undergraduate macroeconomics course. Prerequisites: arithmetic, fractions, percentages, reading simple tables and basic algebra; no calculus is required. Examples focus on interpreting household, business, banking and public-policy decisions using explicit simplified assumptions. Foundational topics overlap with AP and intermediate study, but these scenarios are newly authored rather than relabeled questions from those courses. Growth theory, finance and open-economy mechanisms are introduced without graduate notation. Numerical cases are hypothetical, and course sources guide coverage rather than supplying copied questions or invented empirical findings.
